checks: With common mass zero, the only coupling is zero and both support product and positive output atoms are empty. For positive mass in ambient dimension zero, each supported marginal is the same single physical point of mass M, and every endpoint ceiling there is at least M. The unique coupling has the required ceiling and equality of output laws.

For N≥1 the finite coupling polytope is compact and nonempty. The smooth global uniform Hessian lower bound allows the accepted inverse endpoint lemma, with no absolute-continuity hypothesis. At a positive output atom z the almost-everywhere inverse identities hold there, every slot is one supported endpoint and the tuple barycenter is z. Its whole output mass is charged to the one marginal atom in each slot. This avoids summing over distinct candidate endpoint tuples at the same output.

The set of couplings under the fixed envelope is closed and convex by finitely many linear output constraints, and contains a quadratic-surplus optimizer. For any finite convex test, compact local approximation by smooth mollification plus a vanishing positive quadratic gives convergence uniformly on the finite output set. Every approximant has an unrestricted optimizer in the ceiling set, so the same single-test comparison passes to the limit.

Strict separation of the compact convex vector of test differences from the nonnegative orthant would give nonnegative separating coefficients because the orthant contains all positive coordinate rays and the origin. The linear combination is a finite convex test, contradicting the single-test comparison. Compact finite intersection yields one coupling for the entire family; larger fixed ceilings follow by the original inequality.

The singleton example is sharp: positive M equal to the smallest singleton ceiling is feasible in all slots, and the unique output atom has mass M. If the smallest ceiling is zero, the zero coupling attains zero. This verifies uniform sharpness from ceilings without a claim of pointwise optimality for every fixed set of marginals.
